name: Demas
charge: Forsaking Paul, having loved this present world
summary: Demas is greeted with Luke in the letter to Colossae (Colossians 4:14) and counted among Paul’s fellowlabourers in the letter to Philemon (Philemon 1:23-24). In the last letter Paul wrote, Demas had forsaken him, having loved this present world, and departed to Thessalonica (2 Timothy 4:9-10). No sentence upon him and no repentance is recorded.
offenseFull: Three mentions tell the whole story. First he is a name in the greetings beside Luke the beloved physician (Colossians 4:14). Then he is listed among the fellowlabourers, with Marcus, Aristarchus, and Lucas (Philemon 1:23-24). Then he is gone (2 Timothy 4:9-10). He was not a bystander; he travelled with Paul and warred with Paul, and Paul was in chains under Nero when he left.

The reason is given with no excuse attached: having loved this present world. The teaching reads it as a man who looked around at what the world was offering, decided he had needs the apostle’s company could not meet, and let it overcome him. All that is in the world is the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, and it is not of the Father; the world passes away and the lust of it, and the man that does the will of God abides for ever (1 John 2:15-17). Friendship with the world is enmity with God (James 4:4). And the seed on stony ground is this man exactly: he hears the word and immediately receives it with gladness, has no root in himself, endures for a time, and when affliction or persecution arises for the word’s sake he is offended at once (Mark 4:16-17). The cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the lust of other things entering in choke the word so that it becomes unfruitful (Mark 4:19). The affliction around Paul at that moment was real, and it sorted out who had root.
judgmentFull: No sentence is recorded against Demas. What the scripture supplies instead is the standing rule that answers him. No man having put his hand to the plough and looking back is fit for the kingdom of God (Luke 9:62). Whoever will save his life shall lose it, and what is a man advantaged if he gain the whole world and lose himself (Luke 9:24-25). The thing he went back for was the thing that passes away.

He was not alone in that season, which is the sober part of the case. All they which are in Asia had turned away, Phygellus and Hermogenes among them (2 Timothy 1:15); Crescens went to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia, and only Luke stayed with Paul (2 Timothy 4:11). Christ had already prophesied that many would be offended, would betray one another, and would hate one another (Matthew 24:10), which is why Paul was not undone by it. The application made in class is not comfortable: we have watched brothers and sisters who were called friends, who ate in our homes and knew our families, turn and try to pull the work down, and some who left to start their own assemblies saw them fall overnight, because God does not bless a hand that did that much evil to its own brethren. The sentence on Demas is deferred. Paul left the name in the book, and that by itself is a record.

text.text: Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas, greet you.
There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus;
Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellowlabourers.
Do thy diligence to come shortly unto me:
For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.
Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.
And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.
Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God.
And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness;
And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.
And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.
And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it.
For what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?
This thou knowest, that all they which are in Asia be turned away from me; of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes.
Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry.
And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.
